bull.b: Exceptional revenue growth and a record backlog provide substantial multi-period visibility for expansion. With more than half of the backlog expected to begin customer delivery by the end of 2026, CoreWeave has a durable foundation for scaling utilization and revenue.

Repeated price increases that more than offset cost increases indicate strong demand and differentiated access to scarce GPU capacity. High adjusted EBITDA margins and improving contract economics can support stronger cash generation as the installed infrastructure matures.

Expansion beyond traditional AI-lab workloads broadens the customer base and increases the number of ways CoreWeave can monetize its infrastructure. Managed inference and Forge also create higher-value platform offerings that may deepen enterprise adoption over time.

bear.b: The heavily debt-funded capital structure limits financial flexibility and leaves CoreWeave more exposed to refinancing and interest-rate risk. High leverage can constrain future investment choices, particularly if growth slows or financing conditions become less supportive.

bear.t: Negative Free Cash Flow And CapEx
bear.b: Operating cash inflows are currently outweighed by the capital required to build GPU and data-center capacity. This dependence on substantial ongoing investment and financing increases execution risk and makes sustained growth less self-funded over the next several quarters.

CoreWeave is growing rapidly but has not yet converted that scale into bottom-line profitability, while interest expense is rising sharply alongside debt. Continued losses reduce retained cash available for expansion and increase reliance on future operating improvement and external funding.
